la:verb:prohibeo.gloss: to hold back or before, keep or ward off, restrain; avert; prevent, hinder
senses: to hold back or before, keep or ward off, restrain; avert; prevent, hinder
la:verb:prohibeo.html:
prŏ-hĭbĕo, ŭi, ĭtum, 2 (old forms, prohibessis, ; Enn. ap. Prob. ad (Trag. v. 323 Vahl.):
prohibessit,: prohibessint,), v. a.
habeo
, to hold in front, i. e.,
To hold back, keep in check, to restrain, hinder, prevent, avert, keep or ward off, debar (class.; cf.: inhibeo, arceo).
In gen.; usually constr. aliquem or aliquid, with abl.; alone or ab and abl.; with ut, ne, quominus, or an obj.-clause; also with simple acc.; less freq. with de, the dat., or gen.
With ab: quo illum ab illā prohibeas,: prohibete a vobis vim meam,: praedones procul ab insulā Siciliā,: hostem a pugnā,: aliquem a familiaritate, congressione, patrio jure et potestate,: vim hostium ab oppidis,: se suosque ab injuriā,to restrain themselves, refrain from,fin.: ita prohibendo a delictis magis quam vindicando exercitum brevi confirmavit,; . —
With de: vim de classe, Lucil. ap. Non 528, 10.—
With abl.: cum suis finibus eos prohibent,: itinere exercitum,to impede its march,: hostem rapinis, pabulationibus populationibusque,.—With abl. without an object: non prohibere aquā profluente, .—
With dat.: aliquem alicui,to withhold from one,; cf.: aditum alicui, Auct. B. Afr. 31: captae prohibere nequiret Cum Poenos aquilae,could not prevent the Carthaginians from capturing the standard, (but the gen., ; , depends on the acc. object of prohibere; v. 7 infra).—
With ut, ne, quominus; rarely with quin: dii prohibeant, ut, etc.,: qui tu id prohibere me potes, ne suspicer, Brix ad loc.: quod potuisti prohibere, ne fieret,: ne lustrum perficeret, mors prohibuit P. Furi,: hiemem credo adhuc prohibuisse, quo minus, etc.,: prohibere quominus sumerent, non poterant,: si prohibere, quominus in unum coirent, non posset,: nec, quin erumperet, ubi vellet, prohiberi poterat,.—
With obj.-clause: qui peregrinos urbibus uti prohibent,: qui Bibulum exire domo prohibuissent,: jam se ad prohibenda circumdari opera Aequi parabant,: prohibuit migrari, Veios,: prohibete jus de pecuniis dici,; : audeat Canuleius proloqui, se delectum haberi prohibiturum,; ; : qui Cimbros intra fines suos ingredi prohibuerint,; .—
With simple acc.: Mars pater, ut tu morbos visos invisosque, viduertatem vastitudinemque ... prohibessis, defendas averruncesque, an old formula of prayer in : neque munitiones Caesaris prohibere poterat,: motus conatusque alicujus prohibere,: prohibenda maxime est ira in puniendo,: quod uti prohibitum irem, quod in me esset, meo labori non parsi, Cato ap. Fest. s. v. parsi, p. 242 Müll.: prohibere comitia dicitur vitiare diem morbo, ib.; Cato ap. Fest. l. l.: quod di prohibeant, which may the gods forbid or avert, ; and in the same sense: dii mala prohibeant,; cf.: di, prohibete minas; di, talem avertite casum,; and: deos quaeso, ut istaec prohibeant,.—
In partic., to forbid, prohibit a thing (syn.: interdico, veto): tu modo ne me prohibeas accipere, siquid det mihi,: nemo hic prohibet nec vetat,: lex recta imperans prohibensque contraria,: sed dii et homines prohibuere redemptos vivere Romanos,; ; cf.: Athenis affectus movere per praeconem prohibebatur orator,the orator was forbidden,: prohibitis abstinere,.—
To keep away from a thing for the sake of safety (cf. defendo, II.), to keep, preserve, defend, protect (rare but class.); with ab: a quo periculo prohibete rem publicam,: adultam virginem ab armatorum impetu,.—With abl.: haec damna multa mulierum Me uxore prohibent,keep me from a wife,: magnum civium numerum calamitate prohibere,: tenuiores injuriā,: ad prohibendam populationibus Campaniam,.—With double acc.: id te Juppiter Prohibessit,from that may Jupiter preserve you,.
